title: Minimal Evidence Mapping and Temporal Retention Playbook
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Summary
-------
This playbook defines a minimal, risk-weighted evidence mapping approach and a temporal retention schedule for artifacts that are required to demonstrate compliance across RBAC, authentication, audit logging, and data residency boundaries. It provides concrete retention buckets, owner responsibilities, and incident-oriented collection procedures so teams can produce attestable evidence quickly without retaining excessive telemetry.

Purpose and scope
-----------------
- Purpose: Reduce evidence noise while ensuring the company can produce admissible, forensically usable artifacts for audits, incident response, and compliance reviews.
- Scope: Applies to all Redwood Inference production services, control planes, and customer-facing tenancy metadata. Covers: RBAC changes, authorization decisions, authentication traces, request audit logs, model invocation metadata (non-customer PII), and cross-border residency markers.
- Not in scope: Raw customer content payloads governed by customer retention contracts; those are handled by product retention policies and not duplicated here.

Principles
----------
1. Risk parity: Retain more detailed evidence for high-sensitivity domains (privileged-role changes, key material rotation, tenancy boundary operations).
2. Minimality: Capture the smallest, well-structured set of attributes that prove an event or decision without persistent full payload caching.
3. Timebound: Every artifact is assigned a retention bucket and an automatic expiry; manual extensions require a documented justification and owner approval.
4. Auditability: Retention and deletion operations themselves are logged and observable.

Evidence taxonomy and minimal attribute set
------------------------------------------
Each artifact below lists the minimal attributes to store. Where possible, use structured JSON fields and avoid free-text dumps.

1) RBAC change event (policy change, role binding, entitlement grant/revoke)
- Minimal attributes: event_id, actor_id, actor_role, target_identity, action_type (grant/revoke/edit), resource_scope, timestamp_utc, change_diff (field-level short form), approval_id (if applicable)
- Retention bucket: 7 years for privileged scope; 2 years for non-privileged scope

2) Authorization decision log (allow/deny for a token request)
- Minimal attributes: request_id, principal_id, resource, decision, policy_version, matched_ruleset_id, timestamp_utc, request_context_hash (sha256 of canonical context), response_latency_ms
- Retention bucket: 1 year for high-sensitivity endpoints; 90 days for low-sensitivity endpoints

3) Authentication trace (login, service-to-service token issuance)
- Minimal attributes: trace_id, credential_type, subject_id, auth_method, protocol (OIDC/SAML/API_KEY), outcome, timestamp_utc, source_ip_cidr, geo_marker (region code)
- Retention bucket: 2 years for corporate admin identities; 90 days for ephemeral service tokens

4) Audit log slice for data residency / model invocation metadata
- Minimal attributes: invocation_id, model_id, model_version, customer_tenant_id (hashed), region_code, data_residency_marker, invocation_timestamp, runtime_node_id, kv_cache_hit (bool)
- Retention bucket: 3 years for cross-border sensitive tenants; 1 year otherwise

Retention buckets and actions matrix
-----------------------------------
| Bucket name | Retention period | Automatic action at expiry | Who owns the policy | Notes |
|-------------|------------------|---------------------------|----------------------|-------|
| Critical-Privileged | 7 years | Archive to WORM store (immutable) for 1 year then purge by legal request | Security | Privileged RBAC and key rotation events |
| High-Sensitivity | 3 years | Move to cold storage, audit index preserved for 1 year | Security/Product | Cross-border tenancy markers, model residency events |
| Standard-Audit | 1 year | Delete with verification event logged | Eng-SRE | AuthZ decisions for main API surfaces |
| Short-Lived | 90 days | Automated deletion | Eng-Infra | Service token traces, debug-level request slices |

Ownership and responsibilities
------------------------------
- Security: defines retention buckets, approves exceptions, maintains WORM archive access control.
- Eng-SRE: implements retention lifecycle in the logging pipeline, ensures deletion runs and produces deletion proof events.
- Eng-Infra: ensures provenance fields are captured at generation time.
- Legal/Compliance: approves retention periods for regulatory customers and coordinates legal holds.

Automated retention implementation checklist (SRE runbook)
--------------------------------------------------------
1. Source tagging: Ensure producer services emit a "retention_bucket" and "data_class" field in emitted log envelopes.
2. Ingestion rules: Log router maps stream to retention policy; add index tags for quick search.
3. Expiry job: Daily job runs to move data to appropriate store and issues a "deletion_candidate" event.
4. Deletion proof: When items are deleted, pipeline produces a cryptographic deletion-manifest (hash list + timestamp) and stores it in the WORM index with the deletion_job_id.
5. Verification: Security runs quarterly spot checks comparing retention manifests to stored indexes.

Incident response — evidence collection path
-------------------------------------------
When an incident requires expedited evidence preservation:
1. Incident commander raises an Evidence Hold (EH) ticket in the Incident Tracker with EH_ID.
2. Security toggles the pipeline hold flag for affected tenants/streams; ingestion continues but deletion is suspended for retention buckets implicated.
3. Eng-SRE captures full context snapshots for the specified time window (start/end timestamps) to a secure evidence staging bucket (immutable by default).
4. A preservation manifest is produced: fields => EH_ID, affected_streams, start_ts, end_ts, responsible_engineer, signature (team-key).
5. Legal is notified; changes to hold windows are tracked in the manifest history.

Minimum viable preservation manifest (example)
-------------------------------------------
{
  "eh_id": "EH-2026-0412-4",
  "streams": ["authz-decisions", "rbac-changes"],
  "start_ts": "2026-04-12T10:40:00Z",
  "end_ts": "2026-04-12T12:12:00Z",
  "staging_bucket": "s3://redwood-evidence-staging/EH-2026-0412-4",
  "created_by": "oncall@eng-sre.redwood.com"
}

Note: the manifest above is for illustration. Actual stored manifests are signed and stored in the WORM index.

Exception handling and approval flow
-----------------------------------
- Short extensions (<90 days): Oncall engineer can approve with a 2-way Slack approval recorded in the EH ticket.
- Long extensions (>90 days): Requires Security + Legal sign-off and an entry in the exception register.
- Extension artifacts: justification, retention end date, owner, and reviewer.

Evidence delivery for audits (operational steps)
-----------------------------------------------
1. Request intake: Compliance raises an Evidence Request (ER-ID) with scope and timeframe.
2. Scoping call within 48 hours between Security, Eng-SRE, and Product to map ER-ID to streams and retention buckets.
3. Pull and packaging: Eng-SRE runs an extraction job which produces: signed-manifest, hash-verified archive, chain-of-custody log.
4. Delivery: Archive is staged to a secure transfer location (SFTP or encrypted object share). Legal signs receipt and closes ER-ID upon verification.

Operational controls and observability
------------------------------------
- Metrics to expose: deletion_failure_rate, retention_manifest_generation_lag, evidence_hold_count, archived_volume_by_bucket.
- Alerts: deletion_failure_rate > 0.1% for 30m -> pager to Eng-SRE and Security.
- Dashboards: per-bucket retention heatmap and upcoming-expiry calendar for Legal and Security reviewers.

Sample CLI commands (examples for runbook)
-----------------------------------------
# Mark a stream as held for evidence (SRE)
redwoodctl evidence hold create --id EH-2026-0412-4 --streams authz-decisions,rbac-changes --start 2026-04-12T10:40:00Z --end 2026-04-12T12:12:00Z --owner eng-sre-oncall

# Generate deletion manifest (scheduled job)
redwoodctl retention manifest generate --bucket Standard-Audit --date 2026-08-01

Audit and verification cadence
-----------------------------
- Quarterly: Security performs manifest reconciliation and spot checks.
- Annually: Full audit of retention policy application and exception register reviewed with Legal.
- After every incident: Post-incident review includes a section documenting whether evidence capture and retention behaved as expected and lists any gaps.

Frequently asked questions (FAQ)
-------------------------------
Q: Can teams store additional debug payloads for longer than the bucket?
A: Only with documented Exception and Legal approval. Additional data must be tagged and routed to a named exception bucket.

Q: Who can request deletion verification artifacts?
A: Security and Legal by default; Engineering leads can request for engineering investigations with Security approval.

Appendix: short glossary
------------------------
- WORM store: Write-Once-Read-Many archive used for immutable preservation.
- Deletion-manifest: Signed list of retained artifact hashes proving items were deleted.
- Evidence Hold (EH): A temporary suspension of the retention lifecycle to preserve artifacts for an investigation.
